flows:
Navigate to https://mlyfo.vercel.app/signin?demo=1 then Click the "Sign in" button
Go to https://mlyfo.vercel.app/app/shield
Type "0x7a3f9cE5b801Dd3fA7426C9e0B1f8a5d3e27c4b9" into the "Paste a Solana, Ethereum or Base address" field
Click "Check address"
Assert the result says "Blocked"
Assert the result says it looks like Ada (Base)’s saved address but isn’t
Assert the result is labelled as an Ethereum and Base address

remark: click: Clicking the Sign in button
click: Clicking Click the "Sign in" button
type: Typing address in the address check field
analyze: the result is labelled as an Ethereum address
assert: the result says it looks like Ada (Base)’s saved address but isn’t

summary:
The supplied address has only 39 characters after “0x”, while Ethereum and Base addresses require 40. The application therefore showed an invalid-address block message, so the expected saved-address look-alike result could not appear.
Correct the test fixture to a complete 40-character Ethereum/Base address that is configured as Ada (Base)’s look-alike, then rerun the assertions.
one_liner: The test data is one hexadecimal character short, so Shield correctly treated it as an invalid address instead of an Ada (Base) look-alike.
reason: Checkpoint assertion failed: "the result says it looks like Ada (Base)’s saved address but isn’t"
